name: 24105-decodeheavy-dsv2lite-dp4ep
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3, four GPUs of ONE a3 node (--gres=gpu:4).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=4, expert parallelism ON, so ep_size = dp x tp = 4.
architecture: mixture-of-experts decoder with multi-head latent attention, bf16; ~15.7B parameters total, ~2.4B activated per token.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=64, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 1024 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, seed static 24105.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`: 128 prompt tokens and 512 output tokens per request, min == max == mean on both. EOS is ignored and max_tokens is pinned to 512, so every request generates exactly 512 tokens.
purpose: A long-form creative writing assistant generating 512-token replies from short prompts for 64 concurrent users on four GPUs.
launch:
# Engine: commit a0b26701c91a386e38105816057c1b3e6c1d080f, a source checkout named by
# `configs/env.yaml: venv`.
#
# CAUTION, flat reader: every key must be top-level and every value must fit on ONE line. An
# indented continuation is skipped, and the engine then starts without that key.

model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite

tensor-parallel-size: 1
data-parallel-size: 4
enable-expert-parallel: true

# Per DP rank.
max-num-seqs: 256
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

max-model-len: 2048
# 0.40, not 0.90, and it is a FLOOR rather than a preference. vLLM treats this as a PRECONDITION:
# it refuses to start unless `value x 79.19 GiB` is already free on EVERY one of the four cards, so
# 0.90 demanded 71.27 GiB free x4 simultaneously and was refused on three different nodes today
# (readings of 63.3 / 57.6 / 49.5 / 42.6 GiB free). 0.40 asks for 31.7 GiB and clears all of them.
# It is a floor because it is the LOWEST value that keeps the KV pool above what this engine needs
# to admit its own declared concurrency, so scheduling is unchanged rather than merely adequate:
#   KV/token (MLA) = (512 kv_lora + 64 qk_rope) x 2 B x 27 layers            = 30.4 KiB
#   max-num-seqs x max-model-len = 256 x 2048 = 524288 tok x 30.4 KiB        = 15.2 GiB
#   non-KV per rank (9.15 GiB sharded weights + activation peak at 8192 batched tokens
#     + 67 CUDA graphs + NCCL buffers)                                       ~ 15   GiB
#   floor = (15.2 + 15) / 79.19                                              = 0.38 -> 0.40
# So every rank can still hold 256 sequences at the full 2048 context and the scheduler never
# caps, preempts or recomputes. Do not raise it back to 0.90 and do not drop it below 0.40.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.40
dtype: bfloat16
